A recorded model search

Source: vignettes/research-search.Rmd
research-search.Rmd

The experimental research interface records candidates, evidence, and why an investigation moved between them. R users, Glade, and agents can use the same operations. The execution graph remains available for running computations.

This example uses explicitly illustrative evidence so it runs without Stan. For a real fit and predictive check, run Rscript tools/research-search-demo.R from the repository root with cmdstanr and CmdStan installed.

Normal candidate
  ├─ Record a predictive check without creating a revision
  ├─ Revise P: lognormal candidate
       ├─ Record its predictive check
       └─ Close, compare, then reopen this path

Compare the two candidates, retaining the closed candidate's evidence.

Start with a question 

library(bayesgrove)
h <- bg_init(tempfile("research-search-"))
human <- list(id = "researcher", type = "human")
agent <- list(id = "assistant", type = "agent")

review_rule <- list(
  id = "review-predictions",
  actions = "accept",
  type = "require_review",
  check = "ppc",
  message = "Review the predictive evidence before accepting this candidate.",
  interpretation = "Inspect the features that matter for the analysis question.",
  references = "https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.02439"
)

state <- bg_research_init(
  h,
  question = "How should we model these positive measurements?",
  goal = list(kind = "observable_prediction", focus = "positive support"),
  actor = human,
  mode = "guide",
  rules = list(review_rule)
)

A candidate specifies P (joint distribution), with optional A (approximator) and D (training data). Specifications are plain data. The labels below are illustrative; a reproducible analysis should also retain exact model source, data, and settings, not only labels or mutable file paths.

proposal <- bg_research_propose(
  h,
  action = list(
    kind = "create", label = "Normal",
    components = list(P = list(likelihood = "normal", prior = "illustrative"))
  ),
  actor = human,
  rationale = "Start with a simple candidate and inspect its predictions."
)
state <- bg_research_apply(h, proposal)
normal <- tail(state$history, 1)[[1]]$id

Record evidence and revise

This local helper only shortens the example. Production clients can inspect the proposal’s findings and allowed before calling apply. Apply checks them again.

record <- function(action, rationale, actor = human) {
  proposal <- bg_research_propose(h, action, actor, rationale)
  bg_research_apply(h, proposal)
}

state <- record(
  list(kind = "evidence", candidate_id = normal, label = "Illustrative PPC",
       check = "ppc", utility = "predictive_performance",
       result = list(source = "illustrative", concern = "negative predictions")),
  "The example check raises a concern about predictive support."
)
normal_evidence <- tail(state$history, 1)[[1]]$id

state <- record(
  list(kind = "revise", candidate_id = normal, label = "Lognormal",
       components = list(P = list(likelihood = "lognormal", prior = "illustrative")),
       basis = list(evidence_ids = normal_evidence)),
  "Investigate a likelihood with positive support."
)
lognormal <- tail(state$history, 1)[[1]]$id

A revision replaces the supplied components whole and inherits the others. The parent and its evidence stay unchanged. Changing A or D uses the same operation. A diagnostic or an interpretation adds evidence rather than a revision.

state <- record(
  list(kind = "evidence", candidate_id = lognormal, label = "Illustrative PPC",
       check = "ppc", utility = "predictive_performance",
       result = list(source = "illustrative", concern = "none in this example")),
  "Record the alternative's check without treating it as proof of adequacy.",
  actor = agent
)
lognormal_evidence <- tail(state$history, 1)[[1]]$id

state <- record(
  list(kind = "close", candidate_id = lognormal),
  "Pause this path while considering other alternatives."
)
state <- record(
  list(kind = "compare", candidate_ids = c(normal, lognormal),
       evidence_ids = c(normal_evidence, lognormal_evidence),
       criteria = "Predictive support in the illustrative checks",
       result = list(preferred_for_support = lognormal)),
  "Compare both candidates; the closed path's evidence remains available."
)
comparison <- tail(state$history, 1)[[1]]$id

state <- record(list(kind = "reopen", candidate_id = lognormal,
                    basis = list(comparison_ids = comparison)),
                "Resume this path after the comparison.")

Closing a lineage prevents revisions, evidence collection, and acceptance below it until reopening. Closing does not delete anything or automatically reject a candidate. Comparisons can include candidates from any lineage.

Switch intervention without rewriting history

Record mode preserves actions. Guide adds findings and explanations. Enforce also holds actions with unmet rules. Structural checks apply in every mode.

state <- record(list(kind = "configure", mode = "enforce", rules = list(review_rule)),
                "Require human review before recording acceptance.")
acceptance <- list(kind = "accept", candidate_id = lognormal,
                   evidence_ids = lognormal_evidence,
                   basis = list(comparison_ids = comparison))
proposal <- bg_research_propose(h, acceptance, agent, "Select the alternative.")
proposal$allowed
#> [1] FALSE
proposal$findings[[1]]$message
#> [1] "Review the predictive evidence before accepting this candidate."

An agent can record a review, but it cannot satisfy this rule’s human-review requirement. A human review covers only the evidence it cites. New evidence or a new candidate needs its own review.

state <- record(list(kind = "review", candidate_id = lognormal,
                    evidence_ids = lognormal_evidence),
                "For this example, acknowledge the support check and its limited scope.")
proposal <- bg_research_propose(h, acceptance, human,
                              "Accept for the example's stated goal, subject to further checks.")
state <- bg_research_apply(h, proposal)
state$version
#> [1] 11

A proposal becomes stale after any successful research mutation. Read the state and propose again rather than replaying it. Declared actor identity is provenance, not authentication; a host must establish identity for untrusted callers. Enforce applies to this research interface, not arbitrary R code or legacy bg_run() calls. Existing workflow packs retain their separate behavior.

Reframe without losing earlier decisions

A declared human actor can correct the question or change the inferential goal. Earlier records keep their goal_version; their reviews do not authorize acceptance under the new goal. The evidence itself remains available.

state <- record(
  list(kind = "reframe", question = "How well are the largest measurements predicted?",
       goal = list(kind = "observable_prediction", focus = "upper tail")),
  "Focus the investigation on extreme observations."
)
proposal <- bg_research_propose(h, acceptance, human,
                              "Reconsider the candidate for the revised goal.")
proposal$allowed
#> [1] FALSE

Reopen and share 

path <- h@path
bg_close(h)
h <- bg_open(path)
stopifnot(identical(bg_research_state(h), state))
bg_close(h)

bg_snapshot(), bg_bundle(), and bg_export_report() include research state. The research-search contract lists all action fields and declarative rule types, including specification constraints and evidence requirements. There is no built-in universal model score: comparisons state their criteria and retain their evidence.
